headline: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 at cell-type resolution with a free public API; Mistral thread closed

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's a few minutes past one UTC on Thursday, November twelfth. This is ARA AI News.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The new fact tonight is Google DeepMind walking through AlphaGenome two, a model the show says can finally read more of the genome than the protein-coding two percent.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: On that podcast, the show said AlphaGenome two predicts how DNA variants land at the cell-type level, not from a bulk sample of heart or lung ground up together.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Earlier models in this class stopped at tissue-level calls. AlphaGenome two is built to work at the resolution of a cell type, which is what a rare-disease pipeline actually needs.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The show pointed to the Crick Institute, just down the street. A group there had already found that one variant very likely regulates a gene two hundred ninety thousand bases away.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The show said AlphaGenome two made that same prediction after the fact. That is a retrospective match of someone else's wet-lab work, not a new experiment DeepMind ran on air.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: They are putting it in people's hands. The show said the AlphaGenome family has a public API: install a Python package, and you can run those predictions for free.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Atlas is a no-code website on top of that stack. The show said you do not even need to fine-tune the model on your own data, which is the usability point the episode kept stressing.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The unread stretch is ninety-eight percent of the genome, the non-coding DNA that tells cells how many protein building blocks to produce so the right machines assemble.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: They put a price on not knowing. Only ten percent of drugs make it through clinical trials, they said, mostly because biology still cannot name the true cause of disease.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Nvidia's alleged chip funnel through Malaysia, Anthropic's falling Kalshi IPO odds, hyperscaler capex, and OpenAI's DevDay slate did not move in this inbox. Those storylines still stand.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: We are closing the Mistral and open-weight thread. The twenty VC interview and the Kimi and Ripple weight drops are absorbed, and nothing new arrived, so that story is now settled.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Watch for the AlphaGenome two paper, and whether that free API stays up. On the older files, watch an Nvidia statement on Megaspeed, a filing around Anthropic's November nineteenth window, and CoreWeave's call on those nine billion dollars of prepayments.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That's ARA AI News. We'll be back when the picture changes.
